newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia short of projected '96 GDP - economist.
newsitem.headline: Croatia short of projected '96 GDP - economist.

text.p: Croatia will not achieve the projected 1996 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth rate of 10 percent due to the low level of investment, a leading economist said on Friday.
"(GDP growth rate) will be around five-six percent," Vladimir Veselica told Croatian state radio during an annual economic conference.
"The pace of our investments is slower than that at which machinery wears down... We don't have investments that could be a satisfactory base for an active economic and social policy," he said.
The current level of annual investment totalled only 15 percent of Croatia's investments in 1989, while it was still a republic in federal Yugoslavia.
"Without restarting the economy, and that includes investments as well, it is impossible to bring about an increase of the GDP," Veselica warned.
Croatia launched an economic austerity programme in 1993, slashed the inflation rate and introduced a stable currency, but is still in dire need of foreign capital.
